Reality, Knowledge, and the Triple Constraint

现实、知识与三重约束

Planning for Reality为现实做计划

Craig Letavec, PMP, PgMP, MSP · Waynesville, Ohio, U.S.Craig Letavec（PMP, PgMP, MSP）· 美国俄亥俄州韦恩斯维尔

IT'S AMAZING HOW OFTEN SOFTWARE PROJECTS tend to fall into late, over-budget, off-quality situations. Even in highly touted software shops with international certifications and maturity assessments lining the walls, the trials of managing the very fluid environment of software development are many. The pace of development will naturally vary throughout the life of the project. Sometimes you are ahead of schedule, sometimes behind. Often, project managers seek to control these fluctuations through strict, elaborate project timelines that lay out prescribed task assignments and deadlines. However, they find themselves making multiple revisions to the plan along the way to deal with the dynamic nature of creating software.

软件项目频频陷入延期、超预算、质量不达标，真令人惊讶。即便在那些墙上挂满国际认证和成熟度评估、备受吹捧的软件公司里，管理软件开发这种高度流动环境的挑战也不胜枚举。开发节奏在项目周期中自然起伏，有时超前，有时落后。项目经理常试图用严格、精细的项目时间表来控制这些波动，规定任务分派和截止日。然而，为了应对造软件的动态本质，他们一路上要把计划改了又改。

While the development and execution of a detailed, keenly estimated project plan is important in the success of any project, many software project managers may find some benefit in adding some "reality time" into their plans. The critical chain method uses the concept of "buffers" as one means to deal with inherent variance over the life cycle of the project. Try introducing "buffer time" or "reality time" into your schedule at each phase of your software development life cycle (design, coding, testing, etc.). Buffer time allows for a degree of flexibility within a phase without the need to perform major scheduling adjustments. Think of this buffer time as a time contingency reserve for the phase. The process is fairly straightforward. Look at each phase of your project, consider the total duration of the phase based on your best planning, and then add a buffer task at the end of the phase that has a duration of a percentage of the total phase duration, say 10% or so.

虽然制定并执行一份详尽、估算精当的项目计划对任何项目成功都很重要，但许多软件项目经理可能会发现，在计划里加一点"现实时间"会有好处。关键链法用"缓冲"的概念来应对项目生命周期中固有的波动。试着在软件开发生命周期的每个阶段（设计、编码、测试等）都加入"缓冲时间"或"现实时间"。缓冲时间让阶段内部有一定灵活度，而不必大改进度。把缓冲时间看作该阶段的时间应急储备。做法很简单：看项目的每个阶段，按最佳规划算出阶段总时长，然后在阶段末尾加一个缓冲任务，时长约为阶段总时长的 10%。

— p.108 —

For example, on a 40-day total duration for a design phase, add 4 days of buffer time to the end of the phase, for a total phase duration of 44 days. Will the phase actually take 44 days? Perhaps not, but the "unused" time can then be either carried forward or added to future buffers. As experienced software project managers know, projects may proceed on schedule during the early stages, only to end up dragging on later in the process. Getting ahead of the curve almost always has more advantages than disadvantages.

例如，设计阶段总时长 40 天，就在末尾加 4 天缓冲，阶段总时长 44 天。阶段真会花 44 天吗？也许不会，但"未用"的时间可以结转，或加到未来的缓冲里。有经验的软件项目经理知道，项目前期可能按进度推进，后期却拖拖拉拉。走在曲线前面几乎总是利大于弊。

Expect skepticism the first time you try this approach. "Nonproductive" time is the first thing managers will want to eliminate when they review your schedule. Stand your ground. Make the simple point that you are performing basic schedule risk management. If you have a phase of the project that is riskier than another, add more buffer at that point. You may be able to add less of a risk buffer in other spots on the timeline. Last, make sure that you are not "double-dipping." Double-dipping would be adding extra time at the task level and then again at the phase level. The technique works best when you are not already buffering each of your task durations by routinely adding extra time to each activity to deal with the unknown. Try it. It works!

第一次试这个方法时，要料到会被质疑。经理审查你的进度时，第一个想砍掉的就是"不产出"的时间。站稳立场。简单说明你在做基本的进度风险管理。如果项目某个阶段风险更高，就在那里多加缓冲。在进度表其他位置可以少加风险缓冲。最后，确保你没有"双重计提"。双重计提就是既在任务层加额外时间，又在阶段层再加。这个技巧在你没有给每个任务时长都例行加额外时间来应对未知时，效果最好。试试吧，真管用！

— p.109 —

The Fallacy of Perfect Execution完美执行的谬误

David Wood · Fredericksburg, Virginia, U.S.David Wood · 美国弗吉尼亚州弗雷德里克斯堡

IF YOU THINK YOU CAN CREATE FLAWLESS CODE if you work hard enough, don't be embarrassed. Many others have thought so, too. Unfortunately, it is not possible. Even in theory. Arbitrary logic is hard to verify in the general case and hard, or impossible, to fully test. Drawing an analogy to the bricks and beams used in other construction-related activities, three researchers in the UK recently suggested that software is hard to verify because "there are no good, predictable building blocks. The elements out of which programs are constructed: statements, procedures, or objects, cannot be composed in a predictable fashion." The building blocks of software don't snap together like Legos. They can be put together in so many ways that it is impossible to determine all of the combinations. That may be a decent working definition of Turing completeness. Software is, in a word, complicated.

如果你觉得只要足够努力就能写出完美代码，别不好意思。很多人都这么想过。不幸的是，这不可能，哪怕在理论上。任意逻辑在一般情况下难以验证，也难以（或不可能）完整测试。英国三位研究员类比其他建筑活动中用的砖和梁，最近提出软件之所以难验证，是因为"没有好的、可预测的构件。构成程序的元素——语句、过程或对象——无法以可预测的方式组合"。软件的构件不像乐高那样咔哒一下拼上。它们能组合的方式太多，不可能穷尽所有组合。这大概可以作为图灵完备性的一个不错的工作定义。一句话：软件很复杂。

* Turing completeness: Named after Alan Turing, this is the concept that every design for a computing device could be emulated by a universal machine. True Turing-complete machines are physically impossible, due to the unlimited storage they would require. However, Turing completeness may be attributed to machines that would be universal if they had unlimited storage.* 图灵完备性：以 Alan Turing 命名，指任何计算设备的设计都能被一台通用机器模拟。真正的图灵完备机器在物理上不可能，因为它需要无限存储。但如果拥有无限存储就能成为通用机的机器，可以被称为图灵完备的。

Tracing and verifying arbitrary logic in code may sound esoteric. How about the simpler job of tracing programmer intent? Surely we can talk to programmers and ask them what they meant. Unfortunately, programmer intent is generally lost within a few days of writing a code block, especially when requirements change or are inconsistently documented. Programmers also change jobs, leaving undocumented or wrongly documented code behind. Source code rapidly becomes the last and only forensic clue to programmer intent. Alas, intent can only be imperfectly ascertained from clues like variable names, logic flow, and the occasional comment.

追踪和验证代码中的任意逻辑听起来很深奥。那追踪程序员意图这种简单工作呢？我们总可以和程序员谈谈，问他当时是什么意思吧。不幸的是，程序员的意图在写完一段代码后几天内通常就丢失了，尤其当需求变化或文档前后不一致时。程序员还会跳槽，留下没文档或文档写错的代码。源代码迅速成为程序员意图最后、也是唯一的取证线索。可惜，从变量名、逻辑流和偶尔出现的注释这类线索里，意图只能被不完美地推断出来。

— p.110 —

Bugs will remain part of every software product shipped. We put bugs into software for both bad reasons (like ignorance of language features or poor attention to detail) and good ones (such as conflicting or poorly communicated requirements). Further, bugs are a source of change in software because when they are recognized we refactor the code to fix them, injecting new bugs in the process. Meir (Manny) Lehman was the first to recognize that software evolves during its life cycle, way back in 1969. He later figured out that multiple feedback loops exist within a software development effort, and that those feedback loops influence the process of evolution. They include the injection of multiple (possibly conflicting) requirements and design decisions. Various degrees of programmer understanding of requirements, design decisions, and implementation details contribute to other feedback loops. In other words, the sources of bugs don't have to be logical programming errors. Bugs are also introduced by differences of opinion.

bug 永远是每个出厂软件的一部分。我们把 bug 写进软件，原因有坏的（如不熟悉语言特性、不注意细节），也有好的（如需求冲突或沟通不清）。而且，bug 是软件变化的一个来源，因为发现 bug 时我们会重构代码去修，过程中又注入新 bug。Meir (Manny) Lehman 早在 1969 年就第一个认识到软件在生命周期中会演化。他后来发现软件开发中存在多个反馈回路，这些回路影响演化过程。它们包括注入多个（可能相互冲突的）需求和设计决策。程序员对需求、设计决策和实现细节的不同理解程度，构成了其他反馈回路。换句话说，bug 的来源不一定是逻辑编程错误。意见分歧也会引入 bug。

The Fallacy Of Perfect Execution is the delusion that it is possible to create flawless code with sufficient attention to detail. If that were so, we would all be strong advocates of structured programming techniques. We aren't, and for good reason. Software, at any stage of its evolution, is buggy, extremely likely to change, and inaccurately documented. That insight, simple though it may be, encourages us to approach software differently. It encourages us to develop tools and techniques to incrementally refactor software implementations, requirements, and documentation.

完美执行的谬误，是妄想只要足够注意细节就能写出无瑕代码。如果真是这样，我们都会成为结构化编程技术的坚定拥护者。我们不是，而且理由充分。软件在其演化的任何阶段，都带着 bug、极可能变化、文档不准确。这个洞见虽简单，却鼓励我们换一种方式对待软件。它鼓励我们开发工具和技术，去增量式地重构软件实现、需求和文档。

— p.111 —

Introduce a More Agile Communication System引入更敏捷的沟通系统

Brian Sam-Bodden · Scottsdale, Arizona, U.S.Brian Sam-Bodden · 美国亚利桑那州斯科茨代尔

MOST RETROSPECTIVES OF FAILED PROJECTS place a great deal of blame on communication breakdowns between software project managers, team members, and stakeholders. Project managers are taught to mitigate communication breakdowns between team members, and provide constant, effective communication. The weight of this responsibility sometimes leads project managers to overreact. They blur the line between essential, concrete communications and those where the content-to-noise ratio actually harms project progress instead of helping it. To solve this problem, many software development endeavors are moving toward a more flexible, agile process. The key to agile methodologies is timely communication loops that enable agile teams to respond effectively to unforeseen changes, and quickly reassess and reprioritize project features.

对失败项目的大多数复盘，都把大量责任推到软件项目经理、团队成员和相关方之间的沟通断裂上。项目经理被教导要缓解团队成员间的沟通断裂，提供持续、有效的沟通。这份责任的分量有时让项目经理反应过度。他们模糊了"必要、具体的沟通"和"信噪比反而损害项目进展"的沟通之间的界限。为解决这个问题，许多软件开发工作正转向更灵活、更敏捷的过程。敏捷方法论的关键，是及时的沟通回路，让敏捷团队能有效响应未预见的变化，快速重估并重新排定项目功能的优先级。

How do agile project managers keep communications limited to the essentials? They promote the daily "15-minute stand-up" meeting. It entails developers describing what they've accomplished since the last standup, what they're planning to accomplish "today," and any impediments they foresee in reaching their goals. The negative risk of a stand-up meeting is that it may rely solely on the precision of each developer's self-assessment. The solution? To make stand-up meetings more effective, integrate a task management tool that can show the output of a feature's tests. A tool does not lie about the state of a project's codebase, and testing results are a valuable addition to developer self-assessment. Presenting report data correlating a feature to a set of tests it passed gives a more accurate representation of the state of the feature. For example, results from a continuous integration tool can paint an objective picture of progress. This reduces the stand-up meeting communication to the essentials: reporting of impediments (hopefully, already caught by the task management tool) and unforeseen developments due to edge cases, integration challenges, and bugs/defects. By reflecting these development "discoveries" through a shared, globally accessible tool, developers gain a greater level of feedback precision. Often, unseen connections between features and tasks can be discovered early.

敏捷项目经理如何把沟通限制在必要范围内？他们推行每日"15 分钟站会"。开发要描述上次站会以来完成了什么、"今天"计划完成什么、以及预见到什么达成目标的障碍。站会的负面风险是它可能只依赖每个开发自我评估的精确度。解决方案呢？要让站会更有效，就整合一个能显示功能测试输出的任务管理工具。工具不会在项目代码库状态上撒谎，测试结果是对开发自我评估的宝贵补充。把功能和它通过的一组测试关联起来展示报告数据，能更准确地呈现功能状态。例如，持续集成工具的结果能画出客观的进度图。这把站会沟通缩减到必要内容：报告障碍（希望已被任务管理工具捕获）、以及边界情况、集成挑战和 bug/缺陷带来的未预见进展。通过一个共享、全球可访问的工具反映这些开发"发现"，开发能获得更高精度的反馈。功能和任务之间看不见的联系，常常能被及早发现。

— p.112 —

One typical misconception is that synchronous communications are always more effective than asynchronous communications. Adding development tools and short, asynchronous communication loops can effectively supplement face-to-face communications. At a more general level of feedback, a wiki system can easily keep the vision of the project adjusted to the reality of the development progress. Such a system can also make information available in a timely manner and provide a higher-level channel to communicate to stakeholders-at-large, who might not be interested in the deep, technical details impeding a particular feature's progress. By contrast, a software developer's vision of the overall project can be blurred over time by the minutiae of his daily technical work. A wiki is an effective way to keep a clear, shared vision of the project among all the participants. By attacking the problem of keeping information loops tight and noise-free, software project managers can help avoid the breakdown in communications typically blamed for project failures. A project manager's responsibility and challenge is to streamline the feedback loops at every level of a project.

一个常见误解是：同步沟通总比异步沟通更有效。加入开发工具和短的异步沟通回路，能有效补充面对面沟通。在更一般的反馈层面，wiki 系统能轻松让项目愿景与开发进度的现实保持同步。这样的系统还能及时提供信息，并为广大相关方提供一个更高层的沟通渠道——他们可能不关心阻碍某个功能进展的深层技术细节。相反，软件开发对整个项目的愿景，会被他日常技术工作的细枝末节随时间模糊掉。wiki 是让所有参与者对项目保持清晰、共享愿景的有效方式。通过解决"让信息回路紧凑、无噪音"的问题，软件项目经理可以帮助避免那种通常被归咎为项目失败原因的沟通断裂。项目经理的责任和挑战，是把项目每个层级的反馈回路都精简顺畅。

* Synchronous communication: Participants all participate at the same time, whether in person or by virtual means.* 同步沟通：参与者同时参与，无论面对面还是通过虚拟方式。

† Asynchronous communication: Participants have access to information, but do not have to be physically present and available in real time. Examples include email, discussion boards, and shared folders.† 异步沟通：参与者能访问信息，但不必实时在场。例子有邮件、讨论板和共享文件夹。

— p.113 —

Don't Worship a Methodology不要崇拜方法论

Fabio Teixeira de Melo, PMP · Coatzacoalcos, Veracruz, MexicoFabio Teixeira de Melo（PMP）· 墨西哥韦拉克鲁斯州科阿察科尔科斯

MANY PROJECT MANAGERS GET OVERLY INVESTED in following a methodology, which hinders their ability to manage the project to a useful, praiseworthy completion. If you used a certain format in your last job, studied it in school, or obtained a certification in it, you may feel tempted to rigorously establish all the processes and documents your textbook mentions, exactly as they are described. This is a dangerous pitfall and raises the following issues:

许多项目经理过度投入于遵循方法论，这反而妨碍他们把项目管理到有用、值得称赞的收尾。如果你上一份工作用某种格式、在学校学过它、或考了相关认证，你可能会忍不住严格建立教科书上提到的所有流程和文档，一模一样照做。这是个危险的陷阱，会带来以下问题：

  • Required level of effort. Working thoroughly through all the processes contained in reference materials may require a lot of administrative effort from every team member. Are you sure you have considered all those hours in your time and budget estimates? You certainly don't want to put in place a fantastic set of procedures that document the fact that your project is failing because of the time you took to prepare them.
    所需的工作量。把参考材料里所有流程都彻底走一遍，可能要求每个团队成员投入大量行政工作。你确定在时间和预算估算里算进了这些小时吗？你肯定不想搞出一套漂亮的流程，结果它记录下的事实是：你的项目正因为你花在准备它上面的时间而失败。
  • Executing company's culture. How familiar is your team with those specialized processes? Will you have to train team members? Is that training budgeted? Are they interested? What about functional managers and other company departments with which you will have to deal? Do your processes conflict with formally or informally established company processes and habits? Such conflicts could be a risk to the project.
    执行公司的文化。你的团队对那些专门流程有多熟悉？你要不要培训团队成员？培训有预算吗？他们感兴趣吗？你要打交道的职能经理和其他部门呢？你的流程和公司正式或非正式的既有流程、习惯冲突吗？这种冲突对项目可能是风险。
  • Project focus. The focus of the project manager must be the successful completion of the project, which in a software project is primarily linked to delivering the software. All the project management knowledge you have at your disposal is a means, not an end. Besides, your team will naturally give importance to the same things you, as a project manager, give importance to. If your focus is the full establishment of, and compliance with, all the project management processes, that will be the focus of your team, too. And then who will create the software?
    项目焦点。项目经理的焦点必须是项目成功收尾，在软件项目里这主要和交付软件挂钩。你手边所有项目管理知识都是手段，不是目的。而且，你的团队自然会重视你作为项目经理所重视的东西。如果你的焦点是完整建立并遵守所有项目管理流程，那你团队的焦点也会是这个。那谁来造软件？
  • Virtual or geographically distributed team. If all of your team members are not colocated, it may be very difficult to introduce and enforce mandatory procedures for them to follow. Their hardware and software, as well as other technology, may make compliance with your demands difficult, or even impossible. Narrow your expectations, if necessary, when having remote teams deliver the products or services you need from their small portion of the overall project.
    虚拟或地理上分布的团队。如果团队成员不都在一处，引入并强制执行 mandatory 流程可能非常困难。他们的软硬件和其他技术，可能让你的要求难以遵守、甚至不可能。当远程团队要在整个项目的小部分里交付你需要的产品或服务时，必要时收窄你的期待。
— p.114 —

In the end, no project management book or methodology you feel compelled to follow is more important than your good sense. You should go through a product analysis, a contract analysis, a first approach to a risk analysis, and an interview with your major stakeholders (client and sponsor), and then choose your project management strategy. Try to document it for yourself, with a statement such as "I plan to manage the project this way because…." This will help you adjust your strategy in case the root reasons for your decision change. Based on the needs of the project, you can determine which processes are most important and should be implemented thoroughly, and which processes might deserve a lighter approach. In the end, a good project management plan is all about being effective and keeping it simple.

说到底，没有哪本项目管理书或你觉得必须遵循的方法论，比你的常识更重要。你应该做产品分析、合同分析、初步风险分析、并访谈你的主要相关方（客户和发起人），然后再选项目管理策略。试着为自己写下一句话，比如"我计划这样管理项目，因为……"。这样，当你决策的根本原因变化时，你能调整策略。根据项目需要，你可以判断哪些流程最重要、应当彻底执行，哪些流程可以更轻量。说到底，好的项目管理计划就是追求有效、保持简单。

— p.115 —

Don't Throw Spreadsheets at People Issues别用电子表格解决人的问题

Anupam Kundu · New York, New York, U.S.Anupam Kundu · 美国纽约州纽约市

HAVE YOU EVER BEEN SHOWN A SPREADSHEET with lists of activities to explain your work on a project? Many experienced managers try to use spreadsheet lists as a "silver bullet" for managing and monitoring projects. Tom is an information technology development architect in the online division of a large organization. He serves four or more different stakeholder groups. Since he has a poor ability to prioritize the deliverables for different stakeholders, he ends up annoying or disappointing someone every week. With too many commitments to fulfill, and too few resources on hand, he is always at the center of the resulting conflicts among the groups. Tom and his team are talented IT architects, yet their lack of time and the skill sets necessary to manage stakeholder expectations creates problems for everyone in the online group. The solution? Get a trained software project manager to prioritize and list the deliverables for Tom and his team every week, month, or quarter.

你有没有被人拿一张列满活动的电子表格来解释你在项目上的工作？许多有经验的经理试图把电子表格清单当作管理和监控项目的"银弹"。Tom 是一家大型组织在线部门的 IT 开发架构师。他服务四个甚至更多不同的相关方群体。因为他不善于给不同相关方的交付物排优先级，每周都会惹恼或失望某一方。承诺太多、手头资源太少，他永远处在各群体冲突的中心。Tom 和他的团队是有才华的 IT 架构师，但他们时间不够、又缺乏管理相关方期望所需的技能，这给在线组里每个人都制造了问题。解决方案呢？找一位训练有素的软件项目经理，每周、每月或每季度为 Tom 和他的团队排优先级、列交付物。

* Silver bullet: In folklore, a silver bullet was the only kind of ammunition that would be effective in killing a werewolf, vampire, witch, or other variety of monster. Now, the metaphor can mean a new software or technology that will magically solve all major organizational problems. It can be any solution that is perceived to have far-reaching effectiveness.* 银弹：在民间传说里，银子弹是唯一能杀死狼人、吸血鬼、女巫或其他怪物的弹药。如今这个比喻可以指一种能神奇解决组织所有重大问题的新软件或新技术。它可以指任何被认为具有深远效果的解决方案。

The PM can facilitate discussions with the various stakeholders to prioritize the deliverables. Then, the priorities are evaluated across all the internal customers. This way, not only do the stakeholders have their expectations set correctly, but Tom and his team get a frequently refreshed list of tasks. They can stay focused on developing the most important items on that week's agenda, across all projects. The secret to making this plan effective is not to stop with a spreadsheet list of deliverables for each project. Instead, the PM sets the expectations of the stakeholders by involving them in prioritizing what features or functionalities are the most important/valuable/revenue-producing, given the amount of resources (time, money, and people) at Tom's disposal. Then each group gets feedback regarding how much work it can expect that week, given the needs of other parts of the online division. Communication is the most effective component in planning out the work for Tom's team, especially when the priorities of multiple projects must be established. Perhaps Tom and his team have had an unfortunate experience with one of the stakeholder groups on a past project. With this approach, the "blacklisted" team can continue to get its work completed until time, or a more proactive intervention, helps heal the wounds from the previous interaction. In the end, software project management is about managing people and managing the processes in which they are involved. Interpersonal conflicts within a team and between vying organizational groups are very common. Diversity in ideas, goals, values, beliefs, and needs are the primary strength of teams, not weaknesses. However, they inevitably lead to personal conflicts and conflicts over the prioritization of the workflow through the team. Most conflicts are a threat to productivity and efficiency; resolving them satisfactorily can actually strengthen relationships, foster creative change, and improve results. All conflict resolution tactics depend on proactive communication, active listening, compassionate understanding, and some effective negotiation and/or arbitration. Skilled software project managers are needed—because you can't solve people issues with spreadsheets.

项目经理可以推动与各相关方的讨论，为交付物排优先级。然后，跨所有内部客户评估这些优先级。这样，不仅相关方的期望被正确设定，Tom 和他的团队也得到一份频繁刷新的任务清单。他们可以专注于在所有项目中开发那周日程上最重要的事项。让这个计划奏效的秘诀，不是停在给每个项目列一张电子表格交付物清单。相反，项目经理通过让相关方参与排定哪些功能最要紧、最有价值、最能带来收入（考虑到 Tom 可支配的时间、金钱和人力），来设定他们的期望。然后每个群体得到反馈：考虑到在线部门其他部分的需要，那一周可以期待多少工作量。沟通是为 Tom 的团队规划工作时最有效的组成部分，尤其当必须确立多个项目的优先级时。也许 Tom 和他的团队过去在某个相关方群体那里有过不愉快经历。用这种方法，被"拉黑"的团队可以继续完成工作，直到时间或更主动的介入帮助治愈上次互动留下的伤口。说到底，软件项目管理就是管理人、管理人参与的流程。团队内部和竞争群体之间的人际冲突非常普遍。想法、目标、价值观、信念和需要的多样性，是团队的主要优势，不是弱点。然而，它们不可避免地导致个人冲突和团队工作流优先级上的冲突。大多数冲突对生产力和效率是威胁；令人满意地解决它们，实际上能加强关系、催生创造性改变、改善结果。所有冲突解决策略都依赖主动沟通、积极倾听、共情理解，以及一些有效的谈判和/或仲裁。我们需要熟练的软件项目经理——因为人的问题用电子表格解决不了。

— p.116 —
— p.117 —

One Deliverable, One Person一个交付物，一个负责人

Alan Greenblatt · Sudbury, Massachusetts, U.S.Alan Greenblatt · 美国马萨诸塞州萨德伯里

EVERY DELIVERABLE SHOULD HAVE A SINGLE PERSON who is responsible for its completion. Everyone working on the project should clearly understand who is responsible for the delivery of each item. Actual development of the item may involve a large group of people, but ultimate responsibility for ensuring its on-time completion, and for understanding the technical issues surrounding that item, should be associated with one person. Too often, especially in highly politicized environments, responsibilities are shared, particularly when things are a little fuzzy at the beginning of a project. People like to be responsible for highly visible items that they know are going to be successful. No one wants to be held responsible for something that is sure to be a failure. In the beginning of a project, sometimes responsibilities are shared because a deliverable, and its associated risks, are not fully understood. No one really wants to step up and assume responsibility for a vague task. Sometimes, a deliverable is so juicy that you end up with multiple people who want to assume responsibility for it. Yet, not wanting to rock the boat, management doesn't assign specific responsibility to one person for fear that others will get upset. Either way, you are setting the stage for much larger problems down the road.

每个交付物都应有一个唯一负责人。项目上每个人都应清楚谁负责交付哪一项。一项的实际开发可能涉及一大群人，但确保它按时完成、以及理解围绕它的技术问题的最终责任，应归一个人。太多时候，尤其在高度政治化的环境里，责任是共享的，特别是项目开始时事情还有点模糊。人们喜欢负责那些高曝光、知道会成功的事项。没人愿意为注定失败的事负责。项目开始时，有时责任被共享，是因为交付物及其相关风险还没被充分理解。没人真愿意站出来为一个模糊的任务负责。有时候，一个交付物太诱人，结果一群人都想负责。然而，管理层不想惹事，怕别人不高兴，就不把具体责任派给某个人。无论哪种情况，你都在为以后大得多的问题搭台。

First, if there is a problem associated with a deliverable, one individual who is ultimately responsible for it is much more apt to notify the team early, since she knows she will be held accountable. When time is tight, people have a tendency to assume that anything for which they are not held personally accountable will be handled by someone else. That is how things fall through the cracks. As software project manager, you end up with a crisis on your hands. Second, as the project moves on, it is simply much more efficient for all team members, especially newcomers, to know exactly who to speak to regarding any issue. If you have a question, you want to make sure you are asking the right person—the expert associated with the topic at hand. And, if the expert doesn't know the answer, he will get it for you. You shouldn't have to spend your time chasing down an answer for something you don't fully understand in the first place. Finally, sometimes (all right, often), projects don't turn out as expected. If people aren't held accountable for their actions (or inactions), you'll never be able to fix the problems that occur, and group dynamics will suffer. Few issues are more disruptive to team performance than the group wasting time trying to decide who to blame for failure of a "group" assignment. You don't want to turn this into a contentious means of assigning blame, but rather a means of properly distributing responsibility. And when a deliverable comes in early and under budget (or at least on time and within budget), it's good to know who deserves the praise.

首先，如果某个交付物出了问题，一个对它负最终责任的人更可能及早通知团队，因为她知道自己会被追责。时间紧的时候，人们倾向于认为凡是自己个人不被追责的事，总会有别人处理。事情就是这样掉进缝里的。作为软件项目经理，你最后手上就是一场危机。其次，随着项目推进，所有团队成员（尤其新人）能确切知道任何问题该找谁谈，效率会高得多。如果你有问题，你会想确认自己问对了人——和手头话题相关的专家。而且，如果专家不知道答案，他会帮你找到。你本不该花时间去追一个自己一开始就不完全懂的问题的答案。最后，有时候（好吧，经常）项目结果不如预期。如果人们不为自己的行为（或不作为）负责，你永远修不了出现的问题，群体动力也会受损。没什么比团队浪费时间争论"集体"任务失败该怪谁，更破坏团队表现。你不想把这变成争议性的甩锅手段，而是合理分配责任的手段。当一个交付物提前、低于预算交付（或至少按时、在预算内）时，知道谁该受表扬也是好事。

— p.118 —
— p.119 —

The Fallacy of Perfect Knowledge完美知识的谬误

David Wood · Fredericksburg, Virginia, U.S.David Wood · 美国弗吉尼亚州弗雷德里克斯堡

WE ALL KNOW IN OUR HEART OF HEARTS that we don't know everything. Every day, hopefully, we learn a bit more about our profession, our society, and ourselves. But we simply can't know it all. If we stop learning we fall behind rapidly, especially in the software industry. The idea that one can apprentice to a trade and practice that trade the rest of one's life has gone the way of the dodo. Remember the dodo bird? No? That's the point. Technology, techniques, and the ideas upon which they are built change far too rapidly in our era for any practitioner to know all he or she needs to know at any point in time. We must constantly learn and we must equally adjust to a state of ignorance, which requires us to spend some portion of every project researching the knowledge we need. Why, then, do we persist in pretending that we must, or even can, know everything about a software project during its development phase?

我们心里都知道，自己并非无所不知。希望每天我们都对职业、社会和自己多懂一点。但我们就是不可能全知道。一旦停止学习，我们很快就落后，尤其在软件行业。"一个人当学徒学一门手艺、然后做一辈子"的想法，已经和渡渡鸟一样灭绝了。还记得渡渡鸟吗？不记得？这就对了。在我们这个时代，技术、技巧以及它们所基于的思想变化太快，任何从业者都不可能在任何时间点知道他/她需要知道的一切。我们必须不断学习，也必须同样适应"无知"的状态——这要求我们在每个项目里花一部分时间研究所需的知识。那我们为什么还坚持假装自己必须、甚至能够在软件开发阶段就知道关于它的一切？

The history of software engineering is replete with attempts to control software projects, through carefully bound development and maintenance activities to prevent buggy, failed software. Most such methodologies, such as the classic "waterfall" methodology, presume that with sufficient time and up-front diligence, a software project can be completely understood. Many demand that requirements be set in stone before a line of code is written. What nonsense! Giving up on knowing it all during development, we might think that we can know it all later. Several software development methodologies presume this, such as the spiral or agile methodologies. Iterative development is seen as the key to delivering a software project encoding "final" requirements. Unfortunately for adherents of those methodologies, delivery of a software project is just a comma in development, not a period. Requirements, even when "agreed" upon in detailed upfront design, will change during development. It is impossible to know them all in advance. Multiple requirements often result in inconsistencies, even when they are gathered from a single source. Requirements may even mean different things to different people. Differing interpretations may be due to perception, goals, or language. In order to create a successful software project, we must accept and even embrace these ideas. We do not know it all and we never will.

软件工程史上充斥着试图控制软件项目的尝试：通过严格约束开发和维护活动，防止出错、失败的软件。大多数这类方法论，比如经典的"瀑布"方法论，都假定只要时间够、前期够勤奋，一个软件项目就能被完全理解。许多方法论要求在写一行代码之前就把需求钉死。荒唐！放弃在开发期间全知，我们可能以为以后能全知。几种软件开发方法论都这么假定，比如螺旋或敏捷方法论。迭代开发被看作交付编码了"最终"需求的软件项目的关键。对这些方法论的拥护者不幸的是，软件项目交付只是开发中的一个逗号，不是句号。需求即使在前期详细设计中被"同意"，也会在开发中变化。不可能事先全知道。多个需求即使来自同一来源，也常常导致不一致。需求对不同的人甚至可能意味着不同的事。不同解读可能源于认知、目标或语言。要创造成功的软件项目，我们必须接受甚至拥抱这些想法。我们不全知，也永远不会。

— p.120 —

The Fallacy of Perfect Knowledge is the delusion that it is possible to capture complete, nonconflicting requirements for a software project. The reality is that requirements will never be fully known at any time during a software project's life cycle—not during analysis, development, maintenance, or even (or especially) when the system becomes legacy. Continuous use of the agile techniques of iteration and refactoring into the maintenance phase of the software life cycle begins to address some of these concerns. A fuller understanding of the ways that software evolves may be the next step. Until we have those conceptual tools, use them daily, and accept our ignorances big and small, we will continue to fall victim to the Fallacy of Perfect Knowledge.

完美知识的谬误，是妄想能为一个软件项目捕获完整、无冲突的需求。现实是，在软件项目生命周期的任何时候，需求都不会被完全知道——分析时、开发时、维护时，甚至（尤其）系统变成遗留系统时也不会。把迭代和重构这些敏捷技术持续用到软件生命周期的维护阶段，才开始解决其中一些问题。更充分地理解软件演化的方式，可能是下一步。在我们拥有那些概念工具、日常使用它们、并接受我们大大小小的无知之前，我们将继续成为完美知识谬误的牺牲品。

— p.121 —

Build Teams to Run Marathons, Not Sprints组建跑马拉松的团队，而不是短跑队

Naresh Jain · Malad, Mumbai, IndiaNaresh Jain · 印度孟买马拉德

IF YOU RUN AT YOUR FASTEST PACE for a short period of time—a "sprint" in track and field terms—you burn yourself out. To run a marathon, a team must be disciplined, practice every day, and keep a sustainable pace. When working on software projects, we don't want to run just once and exhaust ourselves. We need to keep going at a steady pace. Sustainable teams are geared toward running marathons and not allowed to just sprint. Building useful software products is not an end in itself. Team members need to learn how to help one another, help other team members realize their true potential, and create an environment that allows everyone to go beyond their limitations. Most teams have a gap in knowing how to do this. Someone needs to play an active role to fill this void. In most cases, the software project manager is the best choice to work on team development. I suggest the project manager target a goal to build sustainable teams. This is a primary way he/she can add extra value to the project. If the project manager focuses on team building and individual growth, on-time and within-budget deliveries will automatically fall into place. This also ensures that teams are self-organized and don't need a babysitter if the project manager needs to guide multiple projects simultaneously. Typically, project managers get caught up in daily fire-fighting tasks. Hence, they don't really have time to strategically build a team. Working with a long-term team development plan ultimately allows the project manager to keep out of micromanagement mode, not only for the current project, but on all future endeavors.

如果你用最快速度跑一小段——田径术语叫"冲刺"——你会把自己耗尽。要跑马拉松，团队必须自律、每天练习、保持可持续的节奏。做软件项目时，我们不想只跑一次就把自己累垮。我们需要以稳定节奏持续前进。可持续的团队是为跑马拉松打造的，不允许随便冲刺。建造有用的软件产品本身不是目的。团队成员需要学习如何互相帮助、帮助其他成员实现真正的潜力、创造一个让每个人都能超越局限的环境。大多数团队不知道怎么做这件事。需要有人积极扮演角色来填补这个空缺。在大多数情况下，软件项目经理是做团队发展的最佳人选。我建议项目经理以打造可持续团队为目标。这是他/她为项目增加额外价值的主要方式。如果项目经理专注于团队建设和个人成长，按时、在预算内交付会自动到位。这也确保团队自组织，万一项目经理要同时指导多个项目，团队也不需要保姆。通常，项目经理被日常救火任务缠住。因此，他们真没有时间战略性地建设团队。用长期团队发展计划，最终让项目经理走出微观管理模式——不仅在当前项目，也在未来所有工作中。

— p.122 —

We need a fundamental shift in the focus of software project management practices so that the PM takes a more strategic role. Leave the tactical things to the programming team. This ensures that the team will take ownership of the project and the software project managers can become true facilitators or catalysts, making sure things are moving in the right direction for the project overall. General George S. Patton said, "No plan survives contact with the enemy." This means project managers need to spend more time empowering their teams to deal with unanticipated changes, rather than trying to get involved in day-to-day coding and architecture decisions. It's foolish for them to think they can fool the information technology team into believing they grasp the intricacies of software development if they do not have a programming background. The team knows immediately that these project managers don't know what they are talking about. A software project manager is like an operating system's kernel. The kernel itself does not do end-user tasks, but it ensures that the end-user tasks are correctly completed by the applications sitting on top of it. Similarly, if a project manager can be a true facilitator and coach who ensures optimal collaboration among the team members, it should no longer be an issue to build self-organized teams ready to run marathons and deliver high-quality software.

我们需要在软件项目管理实践的焦点上做根本转变，让项目经理承担更战略的角色。把战术的事留给编程团队。这确保团队对项目拥有主人翁感，软件项目经理可以成为真正的促进者或催化剂，确保整体项目朝正确方向前进。巴顿将军说过："没有计划能在与敌人接触后幸存。"这意味着项目经理要花更多时间赋能团队应对未预见的变化，而不是试图卷入日常编码和架构决策。如果他们没有编程背景，却以为能糊弄 IT 团队、让团队相信他们掌握软件开发的复杂之处，那是愚蠢的。团队立刻就知道这些项目经理在说什么。软件项目经理就像操作系统的内核。内核本身不做终端用户任务，但它确保终端用户任务被它上面的应用正确完成。类似地，如果项目经理能成为真正的促进者和教练，确保团队成员间最佳协作，那么打造自组织、准备跑马拉松、交付高质量软件的团队，就不该再是问题。

* System kernel: The central component of an operating system. It manages the communication between hardware and software and connects the application software—such as Internet browsers, word processors, spreadsheets, and email—to the hardware of a computer. Memory, processing functions, and input/output devices can thus be used by all applications.* 系统内核：操作系统的核心组件。它管理硬件与软件之间的通信，把应用软件（如互联网浏览器、文字处理器、电子表格和邮件）连接到计算机硬件。内存、处理功能和输入输出设备由此可供所有应用使用。

— p.123 —

The Holy Trinity of Project Management项目管理的三位一体

Paul Waggoner, MBA, PMP, MCSE, CHP, CHSS · Waukee, Iowa, U.S.Paul Waggoner（MBA, PMP, MCSE, CHP, CHSS）· 美国艾奥瓦州沃基

THE SOFTWARE PROJECT MANAGER usually defines the role of each team member at the beginning of a new project, documenting why each team member's skills are vital and the general responsibilities each person should anticipate. However, these documents seldom include an explanation of the software project manager's role during the project life cycle. The challenge for the project manager, especially when working with a new team, is to convey the essence of project management in a 30-minute overview, without overwhelming the team with methodology details. With a busy organization and team members whose first priority is taking care of their primary work assignment, your challenge as PM is to convey, as concisely as possible, one primary point that team members will take away from your meeting: the "Holy Trinity," also know as the triple constraint.

软件项目经理通常在新项目开始时定义每个团队成员的角色，记录为什么每个成员的技能至关重要、以及每个人应预期的总体职责。然而，这些文件很少解释软件项目经理在项目生命周期中的角色。项目经理的挑战，尤其在和新团队合作时，是在 30 分钟概述里传达项目管理的本质，而不让团队被方法论细节淹没。面对一个忙碌的组织、以及首要任务是本职工作的团队成员，你作为项目经理的挑战是：尽可能简洁地传达一个要点，让团队成员从你的会议里带走——"三位一体"，也叫三重约束。

To introduce this core concept, prepare a slide or other visual depicting the triple constraint. This is an equilateral triangle with its three points labeled Time, Cost, and Scope. Together, they outline a space in their center, which is the project Quality. This geometric representation of the project work illustrates that increasing the length of any one of the three sides forces a corresponding change in at least one of the other sides of the triangle. Thus, change also affects the project quality. Point out that this fixed relationship among the three constraints explains why defining scope becomes a critical first step, and a primary limitation. While you may have your own key points depending on the project management maturity of your organization, the type of project you are helming, the maturity of the project management effort, and past experiences with your customers, be sure to cover these:

为引入这个核心概念，准备一张幻灯片或其他可视化，画出三重约束。这是一个等边三角形，三个顶点标注时间、成本、范围。它们共同圈出中间的一块空间，那就是项目质量。项目工作的这种几何表示说明：延长任意一条边，都迫使三角形至少另一条边发生相应变化。因此，变化也影响项目质量。指出三重约束间这种固定关系，解释了为什么定义范围是关键的第一步、也是主要限制。根据你组织的项目管理成熟度、你主导的项目类型、项目管理工作的成熟度、以及与客户的过往经验，你可能有自己的要点，但务必覆盖以下内容：

— p.124 —
  • The importance of each team member's individual participation on the project, which includes assisting with the development of the project plan.
    每个团队成员个人参与项目的重要性，包括协助制定项目计划。
  • Project risks—what they are, how to identify them, and how to create and monitor plans to avoid, mitigate, or respond to them.
    项目风险——它们是什么、如何识别、如何制定并监控计划以避免、减轻或应对它们。
  • Tasks needing further breakdown to define the work to be completed by each member of the team.
    需要进一步分解、以定义团队每个成员要完成的工作的任务。
  • Task assignments, scheduled completion dates, interdependencies of the tasks for the entire team, and the project manager's role in following up to ensure timely completion of the assignments.
    任务分派、计划完成日期、全团队任务间的相互依赖关系，以及项目经理跟进确保任务按时完成的角色。
  • Possible task completion delays, impediments to completing tasks in a timely manner, and the PM's role to assist with removing roadblocks.
    可能的任务完成延期、及时完成任务的障碍，以及项目经理协助清除路障的角色。
  • Communications plans, team member communication responsibilities, and the PM's role as focal point in coordinating plan details.
    沟通计划、团队成员沟通职责，以及项目经理作为协调计划细节联络点的角色。
  • Project status meeting responsibilities and schedules.
    项目状态会议的职责和日程。
  • Outline of next steps you plan to perform as PM as the project plan unfolds.
    随着项目计划展开，你作为项目经理计划采取的后续步骤大纲。

Unless your organization is a "mature" project-oriented business, adding an overview of the basic PM concepts at the beginning of all projects is critical to assist team members in understanding the full extent of their responsibilities and the details of their support structure. This includes laying out your role as their software project manager.

除非你的组织是一家"成熟"的项目型企业，否则在所有项目开头加上项目经理基本概念的概述，对于帮助团队成员理解自己职责的完整范围和支持结构细节至关重要。这包括讲清楚你作为他们软件项目经理的角色。

— p.125 —

Roadmaps: What Have We Done for You Lately?路线图：我们最近为你做了什么？

Kathy MacDougall · Erie, Colorado, U.S.Kathy MacDougall · 美国科罗拉多州伊利

GOOD COMMUNICATION INSIDE AND OUTSIDE THE PROJECT TEAM is a key factor in the success of any project. An important communication tool for all projects is the official project roadmap. The project plan helps your immediate project team chart a course for change at the task level. By contrast, the project roadmap allows the broader stakeholder community to understand the change that will happen at a higher level. The project roadmap is a vehicle that helps to communicate the planned changes, the timeframes for specific changes, and the impact these changes will have on the business. So how does one go about creating a project roadmap? First, enlist the input of top project stakeholders. What features are important to them? What's the priority level of each of these features? Are there things happening within the business that will make it important to have particular features ready by a specific date? Capture the voice of the customer and use this as the foundation for a draft roadmap. Next, create a draft of the roadmap that shows a list of high-level features grouped into a realistic timeframe (quarterly works well typically). For each feature, describe the business value (e.g., reduce time to place an order by two minutes; reduce cost to place an order by $10) on the roadmap. If the business value cannot be described, you should question the validity of including the feature in the project. In short, items without tangible business value shouldn't appear on your roadmap, and they warrant further scrutiny in the form of a cost/benefit analysis.

项目团队内部和外部的良好沟通，是任何项目成功的关键因素。所有项目的一个重要沟通工具是官方项目路线图。项目计划帮你的直接项目团队在任务层面规划变革航向。相比之下，项目路线图让更广泛的相关方群体在更高层面理解将要发生的变革。项目路线图是沟通计划变革、具体变革时间框架、以及这些变革对业务影响的载体。那怎么创建项目路线图呢？首先，争取主要项目相关方的输入。哪些功能对他们重要？每个功能的优先级是什么？业务里是否有什么事会让某个功能必须在特定日期前就绪？捕获客户的声音，以此作为路线图草稿的基础。接下来，创建路线图草稿，列出高层功能清单，按现实时间框分组（通常按季度效果不错）。在路线图上为每个功能描述业务价值（例如：下单时间减少两分钟；下单成本降低 10 美元）。如果描述不出业务价值，你就该质疑把该功能纳入项目是否合理。简而言之，没有切实业务价值的项目不该出现在你的路线图上，它们值得用成本/收益分析进一步审视。

— p.126 —

Once a good draft has been created, get feedback from the project's executive sponsor as well as from the project stakeholders. Provide a live forum for discussion that allows stakeholders to ask for clarity, voice concerns regarding prioritization, and alert the team to items that are missing from the roadmap. These frank discussions build understanding of the project and help to ensure that the roadmap is in alignment with stakeholder priorities. Adjust the draft according to the input received. Ideally, after completing this step, you'll have a roadmap which is supported by all key stakeholders. Finally, shout it out loudly—post the roadmap prominently on the project website, present it to secondary stakeholder groups, and use it as a primary communication tool for the projects. Review the roadmap quarterly to make sure you are on track. Tell stakeholders what has been completed and what will be coming during the next quarter. If delays make it necessary to revise the roadmap, go back to the draft stage and repeat. Communicate the newly revised plan to all involved. This method of creating a project roadmap gives project stakeholders a voice and lets them know what to expect. And last, but by no means least, it affords your team a regular method by which to communicate to others what it has successfully delivered during previous quarters.

一份好草稿完成后，从项目执行发起人和项目相关方那里获取反馈。提供一个现场讨论论坛，让相关方要求澄清、表达对优先级的担忧、并提醒团队路线图上漏掉的事项。这些坦率的讨论建立对项目的理解，帮助确保路线图与相关方优先级对齐。根据收到的输入调整草稿。理想情况下，完成这一步后，你会得到一份所有关键相关方都支持的路线图。最后，大声喊出来——把路线图醒目地贴在项目网站上，向次要相关方群体展示，并把它作为项目的主要沟通工具。每季度审查路线图，确保你在轨道上。告诉相关方已经完成了什么、下季度将推出什么。如果延期使修订路线图成为必要，回到草稿阶段重复。把新修订的计划传达给所有相关方。这种创建项目路线图的方法给项目相关方发言权，让他们知道可以期待什么。最后但同样重要的是，它为你的团队提供一种定期方式，向别人沟通自己在前几个季度成功交付了什么。

— p.127 —
